usdRate.sourceName: Bank of Israel statistics API, representative exchange rate USD/ILS (series RER_USD_ILS)
usdRate.note: Representative rate of 3.118 shekels per US dollar on 30 October 2026; the World Bank 2025 average was 3.45.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: Bank of Israel statistics API, CPI general index, change over 12 months (Central Bureau of Statistics data)
inflation_cpi.note: Consumer prices rose 1.64% in the year to September 2026 (1.5% in August); CBS data served by the Bank of Israel series database. Trading Economics also reports 1.6%.

inflation_projection.sourceName: Bank of Israel inflation target 1-3% (midpoint 2%); market 5-10 year forward inflation expectation 1.93% (September 2026)
inflation_projection.note: Inflation is inside the Bank of Israel's 1-3% target band and bond markets expect about 1.9% a year for years 5-10, so the 2% midpoint is used.

policy_rate.sourceName: Bank of Israel statistics API, Bank of Israel interest rate (series MNT_RIB_BOI_D)
policy_rate.note: The Bank of Israel kept its rate at 3.25% at the 21 October 2026 decision (Trading Economics also reports this).

savings_account_rate.note: Israeli current accounts pay essentially no interest and money is saved in short deposits; no published average rate for a savings account was found. The Bank of Israel website (deposit rate tables) refused access and its open data API has no deposit-rate series that could be located.

fdr_3m_rate.note: The Bank of Israel publishes deposit interest rates on its website, which refused access (bot check); no deposit-rate series could be located in its open data API.

fdr_1y_rate.note: The Bank of Israel publishes deposit interest rates on its website, which refused access (bot check); no deposit-rate series could be located in its open data API.

dps_rate.note: Banks offer monthly-deposit savings plans, but no industry-wide rate was found; Bank of Israel deposit tables could not be read.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: World Bank FR.INR.DPST stops in 2022 (0.44%, before the 2022-2023 rate rises), so it is not used; the current Bank of Israel average deposit rate could not be read.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: Israel has no government savings certificate or retail savings bond for individuals; savers buy tradable government bonds and Makam bills on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.

tbill_91d_rate.sourceName: Bank of Israel statistics API, yield to maturity of Makam (short-term Bank of Israel bills) with 3 months to maturity (series DWH_SRC_0342)
tbill_91d_rate.note: Makam with three months to maturity yielded 3.04% on 30 October 2026; Israel's 3-month bills are Makam issued by the Bank of Israel.

tbond_5y_rate.sourceName: Bank of Israel statistics API, nominal (unlinked) government zero-coupon yield, 5 years, monthly average (series ZC_TSB_ZND_05Y_MA)
tbond_5y_rate.note: Average nominal 5-year zero-coupon government yield in September 2026.

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: Bank of Israel statistics API, nominal (unlinked) government zero-coupon yield, 10 years, monthly average (series ZC_TSB_ZND_10Y_MA)
tbond_10y_rate.note: Average nominal 10-year zero-coupon yield in September 2026; Trading Economics shows the 10-year benchmark at 4.16% on 30 October 2026.

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Israel, income determination (interest income)
tax_bank_interest.note: 15% on interest that is not linked to the CPI (ordinary shekel deposits); CPI-linked interest is taxed at 25%; a 2% surtax applies to capital income above ILS 721,560 a year (2026).

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Israel, income determination (interest income)
tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: No retail savings certificate exists; interest on unlinked government bonds and Makam is taxed at 15% (CPI-linked bonds 25%).

deposit_insurance_limit.note: No deposit insurance scheme for Israeli banks was found; an official source confirming its absence could not be read (Bank of Israel site refused access), so it is not marked absent.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: The Fair Credit Law caps the cost of credit, but its current level could not be read from an official page (gov.il refused access).

equity_return_low.sourceName: Bank of Israel Makam 3-month yield 3.04%; 10-year nominal government yield 4.06% (September 2026)
equity_return_low.note: Low case: equities return no more than a long government bond after tax, after a strong run (TA-125 up 17% in the year to October 2026).

equity_return_base.sourceName: Bank of Israel Makam yield 3.04% (2.58% after 15% tax); TA-125 index record via Trading Economics
equity_return_base.note: Base case: about 4 points above the after-tax Makam yield, in line with the cap; the Tel Aviv market has had a strong 10-year record.

equity_return_high.sourceName: TA-125 index record (Trading Economics); 10-year government yield 4.06%
equity_return_high.note: High case: a fuller equity premium over the 4% long bond yield, as the TA-125 has delivered over the past decade.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Bank of Israel exchange rate 3.118 ILS per USD (30 October 2026)
gold_return_low.note: Low case: flat dollar gold and a stable or stronger shekel.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Bank of Israel exchange rate 3.118 ILS per USD; inflation close to US inflation
gold_return_base.note: Base case: the long-run dollar gold trend of about 4% a year with no expected shekel depreciation, since Israeli inflation is close to US inflation.

gold_return_high.sourceName: Bank of Israel exchange rate 3.118 ILS per USD
gold_return_high.note: High case: strong dollar gold years or a weaker shekel.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: Bank of Israel Makam yield 3.04%; 15% tax on unlinked interest (PwC)
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: short rates fall toward 2% as inflation stays low, giving about 1.5% after the 15% tax.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: Bank of Israel Makam 3-month yield 3.04% (30 October 2026), less 15% tax
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: the 3-month Makam yield after the 15% tax on unlinked interest.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: Bank of Israel 10-year nominal government yield 4.06% (September 2026), less 15% tax
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: locking in long government bond yields, about 3.4% after tax.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: The Capital Market, Insurance and Savings Authority publishes service indices for insurers, but its site (gov.il) refused access, so no industry-wide life claim settlement ratio could be read.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life (risk) insurance is widely sold, but no regulator or other public table of premiums per ILS 1,000 of cover by age could be read; gov.il refused access.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: Hospital care is covered by National Health Insurance through the health funds; no published typical out-of-pocket cost of a major private hospital stay was found.

health_premium_table.note: Supplementary and private health insurance is sold, but no public table of premiums by age per ILS 100,000 of cover was found.

oop_health_share.sourceName: World Bank WDI, out-of-pocket expenditure (% of current health expenditure), Israel
oop_health_share.note: 20.5% in 2023 (WHO Global Health Expenditure Database via the World Bank); older than 2025, the latest available.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: Bank of Israel statistics API, CPI health component up 1.25% and medical services up 2.48% in the year to September 2026
goal_inflation_health.note: Health prices are rising about as fast as the CPI and medical services a little faster, so 1 point above the 2% inflation assumption.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: Bank of Israel statistics API, CPI education component up 0.95% and education services up 2.4% in the year to September 2026
goal_inflation_education.note: Education services prices rise a little faster than the CPI, so 1 point above the 2% inflation assumption.

life_expectancy.sourceName: World Bank WDI, life expectancy at birth, total (SP.DYN.LE00.IN), Israel

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects 2024 via populationpyramid.net
life_table_remaining.note: Secondary source of UN WPP 2024 medium variant for 2026; totals at 60, 70 and 80 are the mean of men and women (only the 65 total is published there).

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP 2024 via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 21.1 (2025, World Bank), 23.5 (2040) and 27.2 (2065, populationpyramid.net/israel/2065/); high fertility keeps Israel younger than other high-income countries.

retirement_age_default.sourceName: Retirement Age Law 2004 (חוק גיל פרישה), sections 3 and 6 (text on Hebrew Wikisource)
retirement_age_default.note: Retirement age is 67 for men; for women born in 1970 or later it is 65 (the transition schedule for women ends with those born in December 1969 at 64 years 9 months). Early retirement age for occupational pensions is 60.

retirement_age_government.sourceName: Retirement Age Law 2004 (חוק גיל פרישה), section 4: mandatory retirement age (text on Hebrew Wikisource)
retirement_age_government.note: The law sets 67 as the age at which any employee, men and women, may be required to retire; it applies to civil servants as well.

retirement_return_low.sourceName: Bank of Israel Makam yield 3.04%; 15% tax on unlinked interest (PwC)
retirement_return_low.note: Low case: short rates fall toward 2%, about 1.5% after tax.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: Bank of Israel Makam 3-month yield 3.04% (2.58% after 15% tax)
retirement_return_base.note: Base case: just below the after-tax 3-month Makam yield, so it does not exceed the after-tax safe rate.

retirement_return_high.sourceName: Bank of Israel 10-year nominal government yield 4.06%, less 15% tax
retirement_return_high.note: High case: part of the money locked into long government bonds.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: Bank of Israel Makam and government bond yields (October 2026)
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case: a balanced mix earning little more than government bonds after tax.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: Bank of Israel government yields; equity base 6.5%; gold base 4%
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: a balanced mix of bonds, Israeli and global equities and some gold.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.sourceName: Bank of Israel government yields; equity high 9%

old_age_allowance_monthly.sourceName: National Insurance Law (חוק הביטוח הלאומי), section 244 (pension 17.7% of the basic amount) and section 1 (basic amount ILS 10,382 in 2026), text on Hebrew Wikisource
old_age_allowance_monthly.note: 17.7% of the 2026 basic amount of ILS 10,382 = about ILS 1,838 a month for a single person, before the 2% a year seniority increment (up to 50%) and dependant supplements; it rises to 18.7% from age 80. Every resident aged 18+ is insured by the National Insurance Institute (a qualifying period of contributions or residence applies), so this is the basic flat pension, not a means-tested allowance.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.sourceName: National Insurance Law, section 245 (entitlement), and Retirement Age Law 2004 (text on Hebrew Wikisource)
old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Paid from the retirement age (67 for men, 65 for women born from 1970) subject to an earnings test until 70 for men (women until their entitlement age): work income above the threshold reduces the pension by 60% of the excess. There is no means test from 70.

gratuity_rule.sourceName: Severance Pay Law 1963 (חוק פיצויי פיטורים), section 12 (text on Hebrew Wikisource)
gratuity_rule.note: One month's salary for each year of work for monthly-paid employees (two weeks' wages for wage earners), paid on dismissal; in practice employers deposit 8.33% (or 6%) of pay into the employee's pension fund for severance.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: National Insurance Law (חוק הביטוח הלאומי), sections 1, 240, 244-246 (text on Hebrew Wikisource)
public_pension_scheme.note: National Insurance old-age pension: residents aged 18+ are insured; paid from 67 for men (65 for women born from 1970) after a qualifying period (generally 60 months in the last 10 years or 144 months in all); the basic amount is updated each January by the CPI. The amount is in old_age_allowance_monthly. Employees also have a mandatory occupational pension (pension funds), not included here.

savings_account.note: Current accounts usually pay no interest; savers use short or on-call deposits.

fdr_3m.note: Shekel deposits can be unlinked or CPI-linked; interest on unlinked deposits is taxed at 15%.

dps.note: Banks offer savings plans with monthly deposits; no industry-wide rate was found.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: No government savings certificate for individuals; retail savers buy tradable government bonds on the stock exchange.

tbill_91d.note: Issued by the Bank of Israel and traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, open to retail investors.

tbond_5y.note: Traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.

tbond_10y.note: Traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.

equity_fund.note: Index funds tracking the TA-35, TA-125 and global indices are widely available.

gold.note: Gold bars and coins can be bought freely.

insuranceRegulator.name: Capital Market, Insurance and Savings Authority (Ministry of Finance)

insuranceComplaints.name: Capital Market, Insurance and Savings Authority, public inquiries unit

pensionScheme.name: National Insurance Institute (Bituach Leumi), old-age insurance

oldAgeAllowance.name: National Insurance Institute (Bituach Leumi), old-age pension

publicHealthCover.name: National Health Insurance (health funds), Ministry of Health
